coverage_gaps: The Layer 1 universe remains strongest in electricity infrastructure and nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks; oil and gas still needs a separate split into upstream services, midstream compression, LNG equipment, refining equipment, specialty valves and inspection/testing.
Renewables remain under-decomposed; a follow-on pass should separate interconnection, inverters, trackers, storage, grid-forming equipment, transmission access and renewable O&M.

Transformer universe is incomplete beyond Hammond Power Solutions; need a dedicated screen for dry-type transformer, liquid-filled transformer, switchgear, busway, protection relay and power-quality suppliers across U.S., Canada, Europe, Japan and India listings.
Public-market expressibility for uranium conversion and HALEU remains thin; Honeywell is diluted, BWXT is a reference leader, and Centrus requires policy and contract verification.
Need verification of analyst coverage counts and market caps to enforce the underfollowed discovery lens rather than relying on qualitative attention labels.
Need customer concentration, backlog visibility and lead-time data for PLPC, ACA, VMI, AZZ and HPS.A before any candidate survives later Serenity layers.
The current candidate list lacks dedicated testing, inspection, certification, utility software/data, interconnection studies and grid-protection software names.

International listings may contain cleaner underfollowed suppliers in conductors, transformer oil, insulation materials, substation equipment, cables and switchgear; these were not fully covered in the supplied Layer 1B extract.

memory_update.text: For the Energy theme, the highest-priority Layer 2 work should start with grid hardware, dry-type transformers, utility structures and second-order grid suppliers before broad utilities or commodity producers.
PLPC, HPS.A, ACA, VMI and AZZ form the initial underfollowed electricity-infrastructure cluster, spanning line hardware, transformers, structures and coatings.

LEU, BWXT and HON form a separate nuclear-fuel bottleneck cluster, but public-market exposure quality is mixed because conversion and HALEU capacity are policy-dependent and not cleanly investable through one pure-play listed company.

Layer 1C remains narrow outside electricity infrastructure; run dedicated Layer 1B expansion for oil/gas services, LNG equipment, midstream compression, refining equipment, renewable interconnection, storage and switchgear.
Next pass should verify market caps, analyst coverage counts, backlog visibility, customer concentration and segment purity before promoting candidates to deeper Serenity evidence validation.

summary: Layer 1C merged universe prioritizes Energy as an electricity-and-fuels bottleneck map rather than a generic sector screen. The strongest Serenity-relevant clusters are grid transmission hardware, dry-type transformers and power-quality equipment, utility structures, second-order coatings/chemicals, and thin public-market exposure to nuclear fuel conversion/HALEU and advanced fuel fabrication. The initial universe intentionally balances reference leaders with underfollowed or second-order small/mid-cap names. Rankings are research-priority scores only, not trading recommendations.
